title: Fifth Word Prescribed Prayer And Avoiding Major Sins Opening Comparison

questions.question: What main lesson is this passage trying to teach about prayer and avoiding major sins?
questions.answer: It teaches that praying and staying away from major sins are basic duties that fit human nature and the purpose for which people were created.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of situation were the two soldiers in?
questions.answer: They were serving during a time of full military call-up and were together in one unit.

questions.question: How is the first soldier described?
questions.answer: He is described as disciplined, careful about his duty, and properly trained.

questions.question: How is the second soldier described?
questions.answer: He is described as inexperienced and mainly concerned with himself.

questions.question: What did the careful soldier focus on most?
questions.answer: He focused on preparing himself and doing his part in the fighting.

questions.question: Why did the careful soldier not worry much about food and supplies?
questions.answer: He understood that providing those things was the responsibility of the government.

questions.question: Besides training and fighting, what small support tasks did the careful soldier still do?
questions.answer: He helped with simple camp duties like preparing cookware, cleaning eating tools, and bringing them where needed.

questions.question: When asked what he was doing, how did the careful soldier understand those chores?
questions.answer: He saw them as service connected to the state, not as a personal job just to earn food.

questions.question: What does this show about the careful soldier’s attitude toward his role?
questions.answer: It shows that he knew his real mission and did not confuse side tasks with his main duty.

questions.question: According to the passage, what are people asked to understand through the soldier comparison?
questions.answer: They are asked to understand that the daily prayers and staying away from grave sins are natural and proper duties for human beings.

questions.question: Where were the two soldiers placed?
questions.answer: They were in the same regiment during a public military mobilization.

questions.question: What personal quality made the first soldier act differently from the second?
questions.answer: He had a strong sense of responsibility and took his duty seriously.

questions.question: What was the second soldier mainly thinking about?
questions.answer: He was mainly thinking about his own food and provisions.

questions.question: What belief guided the first soldier’s calm attitude about being fed and equipped?
questions.answer: He believed the authorities would take care of his basic needs.

questions.question: How far did that trust go if he became too weak or sick?
questions.answer: He believed they would even care for him very closely if necessary.

questions.question: What did the first soldier know was his own main responsibility?
questions.answer: His own responsibility was to prepare himself well and take part in the battle.

questions.question: Did the first soldier completely ignore supply-related work? Explain.
questions.answer: No. He still helped with certain practical tasks when they were part of his assigned work.

questions.question: What important difference is shown between “doing service” and “working for one’s living” in the passage?
questions.answer: The passage shows that some work is done as part of one’s duty and service, not because a person is the real provider for himself.

questions.question: What two actions are linked together as part of true human responsibility in this passage?
questions.answer: Performing the prescribed prayers and avoiding serious sins.

questions.question: Why does the passage use a comparison with soldiers?
questions.answer: It uses a familiar example to make the lesson about duty, trust, and obedience easier to understand.

questions.question: What was special about the time when the story happened?
questions.answer: It was a time when people had been called up generally for military service.

questions.question: What can be understood from calling one soldier “conscientious”?
questions.answer: It means he was reliable, careful, and committed to doing what he was supposed to do.

questions.question: What can be understood from calling the other soldier “self-centred”?
questions.answer: It means he mostly cared about himself instead of the larger mission or shared duty.

questions.question: Why did the dutiful soldier not make obtaining food his main concern?
questions.answer: He knew that his needs would be provided by those in charge, while his own duty was something else.

questions.question: Name one example of camp work the dutiful soldier carried out.
questions.answer: He cleaned the eating utensils.

questions.question: What answer did the dutiful soldier give when he was asked what he was doing?
questions.answer: He said he was carrying out service tasks for the state.

questions.question: What does his answer tell us about how he viewed his daily chores?
questions.answer: It shows he viewed them as part of obedience and responsibility, not as chasing personal gain.

questions.question: What does the passage say is suitable for a human being because of how people were created?
questions.answer: It says that prayer and keeping away from major wrongdoing suit human beings and their created purpose.

questions.question: How many soldiers are mentioned in the comparison?
questions.answer: Two soldiers are mentioned.

questions.question: What two main things occupied the mind of the first soldier?
questions.answer: His preparation and the struggle he had to take part in.

questions.question: According to the first soldier, whose duty was it to provide food, clothing, and treatment?
questions.answer: It was the duty of the state.

questions.question: What did the first soldier believe would happen if he became ill?
questions.answer: He believed he would be treated and cared for.

questions.question: How did the first soldier combine trust with action?
questions.answer: He trusted that his needs would be provided, but he still did the duties assigned to him.

questions.question: What mistake did the first soldier avoid making about his work?
questions.answer: He avoided treating his side chores as if they were his real purpose in life.

questions.question: What Qur’anic message appears at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It says that Allah is with those who are mindful of Him and those who do good.

questions.question: What kind of man was the first soldier in character?
questions.answer: He was serious about responsibility and acted with discipline.

questions.question: What kind of man was the second soldier in character?
questions.answer: He was immature in duty and mostly concerned with himself.

questions.question: Why did the first soldier not become anxious over daily provisions?
questions.answer: He knew that these were already under the care of those who commanded him.

questions.question: What examples in the passage show that the first soldier still worked when needed?
questions.answer: He handled kitchen-related tasks and cleaned up the soldiers’ eating equipment.

questions.question: If someone asked him why he was doing that work, what was his understanding?
questions.answer: He understood it as service connected to his official duty.

questions.question: What wrong way of thinking did he reject about those chores?
questions.answer: He rejected the idea that he was mainly laboring just to secure his own living.

questions.question: What does the passage say about prayer in relation to human nature?
questions.answer: It says prayer fits human nature and is a proper outcome of why humans were created.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with prayer as something a person should avoid?
questions.answer: It connects prayer with staying away from major sins.

questions.question: What setting is used to explain this lesson?
questions.answer: The lesson is explained through an example from military service.

questions.question: What difference in attitude appears between the two soldiers right away?
questions.answer: One takes duty seriously, while the other thinks mainly about himself.

questions.question: What did the responsible soldier understand about food and equipment?
questions.answer: He understood that these needs would be provided by the state.

questions.question: What did he see as his essential mission?
questions.answer: He saw his essential mission as being trained and taking part in the fight.

questions.question: Give two examples of the small duties he performed besides his main mission.
questions.answer: He prepared cooking pots and washed the soldiers’ eating containers.

questions.question: Why is his response about those chores important?
questions.answer: It shows that he kept the right order of priorities and did not confuse support work with his true assignment.

questions.question: Based on the whole comparison, what kind of person is being praised?
questions.answer: A person who knows his duty, acts responsibly, and trusts the One in charge for his needs is being praised.
